$comment: Parity policy for the shared VfNavMenu cases. Plain data: no DSL, no waiver engine. It starts empty and stays empty. What the Razor adapter cannot represent - a consumer that does not write the emitted value back, a router - is a declared platform divergence or outside the catalog, never an approval.

classifications.exact: Must match literally across every target. Structure, canonical classes, native attributes, the listbox's inline position and min-width, visible text, accessible names and states, live state, ownership, relationships, focus, the value log, the form entries and the transitions.
classifications.semantic: Framework mechanics may differ; the observable meaning must not. How content is composed, how state is stored, how a renderer marks its own output, which literal a generated id has, how an adapter anchors its teleported content.
classifications.framework-specific: Historical behaviour of one adapter that the other is not required to reproduce. Narrow, named, and covered by its own test.

notCompared.$comment: Recorded so a reviewer can see what is deliberately outside the comparison, without leaving dead dimensions that look like live protection. Nothing here is a waiver: the extractor never produces these differences in the first place.
notCompared.attributeOrder: Attributes are extracted into a sorted map, so serialisation order cannot produce a difference.
notCompared.rendererMarkers: Vue scope attributes (data-v-*), the Razor ownership marker, the Razor adapter's configuration (data-vf-razor-nav-menu-*, the tree structure, every li's index path) and the inert <template data-vf-razor-nav-menu="collapse"> elements holding each branch's children are dropped by scripts/parity/extract.mjs. What the templates hold is compared the moment the controller renders it.
notCompared.eventTransport: Vue emits update:modelValue, change and select; the Razor controller dispatches one bubbling vf-nav-menu:change with { value }. What is compared is the neutral log each fixture keeps from readiness on - one entry per announced change, repeats included - as interaction.events.
notCompared.styleSerialisation: Vue writes --vf-nav-menu-level and the transition hooks' declarations through the CSSOM; the Razor server writes the level as attribute text and its controller writes the hooks through the CSSOM. The extractor parses every style through the browser and compares the declarations.

platformDivergences.description: Vue: with `modelValue` given, a leaf click emits update:modelValue, change and select and moves nothing until the parent writes the value back. Razor: `model-value` is the initial value only - read exactly as `default-value` - and the controller moves the active value itself and dispatches vf-nav-menu:change.
platformDivergences.reason: A server-rendered menu has no parent in the page to emit a request to and wait on. The same divergence as VfTabs', VfSelect's and VfStepper's.
platformDivergences.comparedAs: nav-menu/controlled and nav-menu/interaction-controlled: the Vue fixture writes update:modelValue back (v-model), the Razor adapter applies the value directly, and all three targets must land on the same tree, events, focus and accessibility tree.
platformDivergences.vueHalfCoveredBy: packages/core/src/components/nav-menu/VfNavMenu.characterization.spec.ts (events: controlled - the click emits but the active value stays until the parent writes it back; dropping modelValue falls back to an internal value a controlled click never wrote)
platformDivergences.razorHalfCoveredBy: packages/razor/tests/Components/NavMenuComponentTest.php (model-value is the initial value and beats the default) and scripts/ci/check-razor-browser.mjs (a leaf click moves aria-current and dispatches vf-nav-menu:change)
platformDivergences.mutationCoveredBy: scripts/baseline/input-mutations.mjs#nav-menu-controlled-self-update - the Razor reading applied to the Vue component - is detected by the characterization suite

outsideTheCatalog.$comment: Behaviour that is part of the contract and deliberately not represented as a parity case, each with where it is covered instead.
outsideTheCatalog.routerLink: An item `to` hands off to whatever is registered as RouterLink, with target, rel, classes, the level style, aria and the click listener, and renders Vue's literal unresolved element with nothing registered. Vue-only: the Razor adapter refuses `to` by name. Covered by the characterization suite (router branch) and NavMenuComponentTest::testTheRouterBranchIsRefusedByName.
outsideTheCatalog.reversals: Closing while entering and reopening while leaving happen inside two animation frames, faster than a scenario step settles. Covered by the characterization suite (transition) and scripts/ci/check-razor-browser.mjs (reversals).
outsideTheCatalog.transitionTiming: The end on a computed duration other than the reduced-motion one, on transitionend counting and on a bubbled transitionend: the characterization suite and scripts/ci/check-razor-browser.mjs (40ms and 10s durations). The parity run compares the frame-sampled life of every collapse under reduced motion.
outsideTheCatalog.reactiveProps: items, variant and modelValue changed by a parent after mount: Vue-only, characterised; the Razor adapter renders once.
outsideTheCatalog.focusOnCollapse: Focus inside a subtree that leaves is lost to the body when it is removed: characterised; a pointer collapse moves focus to the branch first.
outsideTheCatalog.windowResizeFallback: Without ResizeObserver the reference listens to window resize: characterised; no parity browser lacks ResizeObserver.
outsideTheCatalog.targetBlankClicks: A _blank link is compared statically and never clicked: a click would open a second page.

dom.structure.description: An unexpected element, a missing item, a group rendered as a button, a branch rendered as a link, a collapse rendered while closed or left after its leave, a nested list in the wrong place. Never approvable.

dom.canonicalClasses.description: The node, item, group, collapse, icon and root modifiers - level, expanded, active, ancestor-active, disabled, top, icon-offset, branch, simple, variant and sidebar-compact.

dom.nativeAttributes.description: type, disabled, tabindex, href, target, rel, title and the inline --vf-nav-menu-level, parsed by the browser.

dom.text.description: Visible text: the displayed label (or placeholder, or nothing under a floating label), each option's label, the field label, description and error.

dom.aria.description: aria-expanded on every branch, aria-current on every current leaf, aria-disabled on a disabled link, aria-label on the nav, aria-hidden on the probe and the glyph slots.

dom.productData.description: data-vf-filled on the trigger while the model is non-empty, and a consumer data-testid.

dom.relationships.description: The reference writes no id reference: no branch aria-controls. An adapter that wrote one would differ here.

dom.actionPresence.description: Whether each button is operable: the trigger of a disabled select and a disabled option are inoperable on every target.

dom.wrapperPresence.description: Present so the comparator has a classification for it. A select has no wrapper either adapter may add.

dom.inertAction.description: Present for the same reason. A select renders no inert action.

style.geometry.description: width, height, padding, border width and radius, font size and line height of the wrapper, the trigger, the value, the chevron, the clear button and an in-place listbox.

style.colour.description: colour, background colour and border colour of the same elements.

visual.description: Clipped screenshot of the case root in its initial state, per theme.

visual.postInteraction.description: Clipped screenshot after the interaction, per theme, covering the case root and every listbox it owns wherever it is.

a11y.role.description: Computed role of the trigger (button), the clear button, the listbox and its first, selected and disabled options, read where the listbox is; the aria-hidden chevron is absent.

a11y.name.description: Accessible name of the trigger (its label, or the consumer's aria-label, or the field label), of the clear button, of the listbox (its trigger, through aria-labelledby) and of each read option.

a11y.states.description: focusable, disabled, expanded, hasPopup, invalid and selected as exposed to assistive tech, before and after an interaction.

ownership.controls.description: The component-owned controls: every trigger, the clear button while shown and every option of an open listbox, with tag, role, aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, aria-selected, disabled, tabindex and name; the consumer count beside them and the totals they add up to.

interaction.state.description: The live state after a scenario, per instance: aria-expanded, the trigger's label and classes, the listbox's place, classes, role and options, its geometry and scroll, every listbox in <body> by what names it, the field and a popover around the select, and the transitions.

interaction.events.description: The neutral value log the fixture recorded from readiness on, with the instance and the value. A missing, duplicated or reordered emission differs.

interaction.convergence.description: Whether a closing gesture's DOM equals the target's own render of the closed case it lands on. A leave that left a listbox behind, a stale label or a clear button that did not swap back differs.

interaction.focus.description: Where focus is after the scenario - a trigger, the clear button, an option (by label), another control, the body - and which instance holds it.

interaction.relationships.description: Whether each trigger's aria-controls reaches a listbox labelled by that trigger, on the live DOM, and that nothing carries aria-activedescendant.

interaction.value.description: The hidden input per instance (name, value, disabled, first in the wrapper), the entries of the form around the case and its validity.

interaction.selection.description: Present for the shared comparator. A select carries no caret.

interaction.wrapperPresence.description: Present for the shared comparator. A select renders no wrapper that could appear on one side only.

historicalQuirks.description: In single mode a sibling group is not a branch and is skipped whole: the branches inside it stay open.
Group values are part of the ancestry: a group around the current item carries vf-nav-menu__node--expanded on its li.
A branch with href, target or to is a button and drops them.
href '' is a link: the link test is definedness.
A disabled link that is current carries aria-current beside aria-disabled.
Clicking the current item announces it again.
Closing a branch keeps its descendants expanded; reopening shows them at once, without a transition.
The ancestry is the first match in document order; every rendered match is current.
No component keyboard handling: arrows are not prevented, Enter and Space are native activation.
